title: Pay of $2.50 a night and tips at the Spinning Wheel
summary: Early-thirties Kansas City work paid little; nine to five for $2.50 plus tips, with visits back and forth to Basie at the Reno.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, now, it's the late twenties in the Gillis Theatre, what were some of the other -- from there -- here in Kansas City things really started to go, didn't they, in the 1930s, in the early thirties. You really -- you weren't out of work very much, or any other musicians were you?
Oh, no. We wasn't making any money amounting to anything.
Tell me about the money. How were you paid?
We would play 9:00 o'clock until 5:00 in the morning off the Spinnin' Wheel (Inaudible). And your highest payment was $2.50 --
And you played for tips I guess mostly.
That's right, tips were great, though.

Yeah. And they were awful nice to us you understand, because we played all the stuff. And Basie was right down the street at the Reno Arena then, and during the intermission I'd go down and see Basie, when he'd have an inter-
mission he'd come to see me.
